newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline prompt values jump, Aug onwards flat.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline prompt values jump, Aug onwards flat.

text.p: A particularly quiet start to gasoline trading on Friday saw a single reported Eurograde barge deal for first half August at $196.50, reflecting little change from Thursday, as July barrels were talked $4 up in the wake of a late Thursday deal at $202.

The Scandinavian player who bought at $202 on Thursday indicated he would be happy to buy again at that level, as a seller indicated he would seek $204 during Friday, although wider market interest was very lacklustre.

The $7 backwardation therefore seen emerging between balance-of-July and first half August barges was reflected by a flat or slightly weaker swap scene, where August, September and October values were placed by lunchtime around $195.50, $189 and $184 respectively.
A U.S. oil refiner confirmed it had sold a 20,000 tonne CIF NWE cargo on Thursday in line with published values and for August 5-10 shipment.
The fate of a separate CIF Thames cargo was unclear in a cargo market that remains tight but, according to one producer, heading for decline from mid-August.
